entities.summary: Terrah Jerrod Mustaf was an American professional basketball player. In high school, he was a three-time Parade All-American. He participated in the Capital Classic and McDonald's All-American Game. Mustaf played four seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA), after being drafted 17th in the 1990 NBA draft. After his girlfriend was murdered, Mustaf came under suspicion when his cousin was convicted of the crime. Mustaf later left the United States to play professionally in Europe. After returning to the United States, Mustaf committed himself to charitable causes for youth in Maryland.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Mustaf's involvement in his girlfriend's murder and subsequent conviction of his cousin had a significant impact on his personal life and career. His decision to leave the US and play professionally in Europe also led to him committing himself to charitable causes for youth in Maryland.
